ees.title: EES check: how long can you stay in Schengen? The Entry/Exit System explained
ees.metaDesc: The EU Entry/Exit System (EES) has replaced passport stamps at Schengen external borders since 10 April 2026: photo and fingerprints, who is exempt, and the official tool to check how many days you have left.
ees.answer: The Entry/Exit System (EES) is the EU's digital register of non-EU travellers on short stays. It has been fully running at the external borders of the 29 European countries that use it since 10 April 2026: on your first crossing your face photo and/or fingerprints are recorded and your passport is no longer stamped. It applies whether or not you need a visa, there is nothing to apply or pay for, and an official online tool shows how many of your 90 days in any 180 days you have left.

sections.h: Who is registered in the EES?
p: Every non-EU national travelling for a short stay (up to 90 days in any 180-day period) to the countries using the EES, both travellers who need a Schengen visa and visa-exempt travellers such as US, UK or Mexican citizens. The 29 countries are the Schengen states: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden and Switzerland.

Not registered: nationals of these countries and of Cyprus and Ireland; holders of residence permits and long-stay (D) visas; nationals of Andorra, Monaco and San Marino and holders of Vatican passports; non-EU family members of EU citizens who hold a residence card. In Cyprus and Ireland passports are still stamped by hand.

list: First crossing since the EES started: you give your personal data, officers take a photo of your face and/or scan your fingerprints, and a digital file is created. Your passport is not stamped.
It can be quicker if you register some data in advance at a self-service kiosk at the border or in a mobile app, where the country offers one; you still meet a border officer.
Later crossings: your photo and/or fingerprints are only verified. With a biometric passport you may be able to use self-service gates.
If you refuse to give your fingerprints or photo, you are refused entry.
All other entry conditions (valid passport, visa if required, money, accommodation, return ticket) still apply.

sections.h: EES check: how many days do you have left?
p: The EU's official online tool at travel-europe.europa.eu/ees/check-how-long-you-can-stay tells you whether your entry is allowed ('OK' or 'not OK') and how many days of your authorised stay remain. You enter your travel document type and number, the three-letter code of the issuing country (for example USA, GBR, IND, TUR), the country you are visiting and, depending on your case, your planned entry and/or exit date. It is free.

The count does not include any time spent in the Schengen area that began before 10 April 2026, so if you were there earlier, add those days yourself (our Schengen 90/180 calculator helps). You can also ask the border officer how many days you have left.

sections.h: How long is your data kept and what about overstays?
list: Records of entries, exits and refusals: 3 years.
Your personal file: 3 years and 1 day after your last exit.
If no exit is recorded: 5 years from the end of your authorised stay.
If you stay longer than allowed, the system automatically flags you as an overstayer, and border, immigration and visa authorities can see it, which can affect future visas and entries.

p: The EES only records border crossings. ETIAS is a separate online travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers that is not in operation yet; see our ETIAS guide for its status.

faq.q: Do I have to apply or pay for the EES?
faq.a: No. There is no application and no fee; you are registered automatically at the border the first time you enter a country using the EES.

faq.q: How do I check how long I can stay in Schengen with the EES?
faq.a: Use the official tool at travel-europe.europa.eu/ees/check-how-long-you-can-stay with your passport number, issuing country and destination; it shows 'OK' or 'not OK' and your remaining days. Days from stays that began before 10 April 2026 are not included.

faq.q: Are passports still stamped?
faq.a: Not in the 29 countries using the EES; your entries and exits are recorded digitally. Cyprus and Ireland still stamp passports by hand.

faq.q: Does the EES apply if I have a Schengen visa?
faq.a: Yes. It applies to all non-EU short-stay travellers, with or without a visa. Holders of residence permits or long-stay visas are not registered.

etias.title: What is ETIAS? Europe's new travel authorisation: no start date yet
etias.metaDesc: ETIAS is not in operation yet and the EU no longer gives a launch date; it will be announced several months ahead. €20 fee, 3-year validity, who must apply, and the EES border checks already in place.
etias.answer: ETIAS is an online travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers to Europe. It is not in operation yet: the European Commission has dropped its earlier last-quarter-2026 target and says the start date will be announced several months in advance. Until then you do not need ETIAS, and any site taking applications now is not official. Once it starts it will cost €20 and be valid for 3 years. Travellers who already need a Schengen visa keep applying for a visa instead.

p: Citizens of countries that can enter the Schengen area without a visa, such as the US, Canada, the UK, Australia, Japan and the Gulf states. ETIAS will cover the Schengen countries and Cyprus.
If your nationality needs a Schengen visa, ETIAS does not apply to you; you keep applying for a visa.

list: Fee: €20 (free under 18 and over 70, but they must still apply).
Valid for 3 years or until your passport expires, whichever comes first.
The 90 days in any 180 days rule stays the same.
First 6 months are a transition period: nobody is refused entry only for lacking ETIAS; a further 6-month grace period follows.

p: Apply only on the official ETIAS website or app; it takes a few minutes. You need your passport, personal details and a few security questions. Most applications are expected to be approved within minutes. Third-party sites charge an extra service fee for the same thing.

Separately, the EU Entry/Exit System (EES) has been fully running at all Schengen external borders since 10 April 2026. Non-EU travellers give fingerprints and a facial image on their first entry, and passports are no longer stamped.

faq.q: When does ETIAS start?
faq.a: There is no date yet. The EU removed its last-quarter-2026 target; the start will be announced several months in advance. You do not need ETIAS for now.

faq.q: Is ETIAS a visa?
faq.a: No. It is a pre-travel security check for people who can already travel visa-free; no consulate visit or appointment is needed.

faq.q: Do children need ETIAS?
faq.a: Yes, every traveller needs one, but under-18s pay no fee.

uk_eta.title: UK ETA: price, validity and who needs it (2026)
uk_eta.metaDesc: The UK ETA has been mandatory since 25 February 2026. It costs £20, lasts 2 years and covers stays of up to 6 months. Who needs it, who needs a visa instead.
uk_eta.answer: The UK ETA is a mandatory online permission for visitors from visa-exempt countries. Since 25 February 2026 travellers without one can be refused boarding. It costs £20, is valid for 2 years and allows stays of up to 6 months per visit.

p: Nationals of countries that can visit the UK without a visa, including all EU countries, the US, Canada, Australia, Japan and the Gulf states. British and Irish citizens, and people with a valid UK visa or residence status, do not need one.
If your nationality needs a UK visa (for example Turkey, India or China), you apply for a Standard Visitor visa instead.

list: £20 per person (since 8 April 2026; it was £16 before).
Valid for 2 years or until your passport expires.
Stay up to 6 months per visit, with multiple visits allowed.
A new passport means a new ETA.

p: Apply in the official UK ETA app or on GOV.UK. You need your passport, a photo of your face and a few answers. A decision usually comes within 3 working days, so do not leave it to the last minute.

list: Children and babies need their own ETA.
Passengers transiting airside without passing UK border control currently do not need an ETA (temporary exemption).
EU national ID cards are not accepted for UK entry, except for people with EU Settlement Scheme status.
Since 25 February 2026 airlines refuse boarding without an ETA.

faq.q: Do EU citizens need a UK ETA?
faq.a: Yes. Since 2 April 2025 European visitors need an ETA, and it has been strictly enforced since 25 February 2026.

faq.q: How long does an ETA take?
faq.a: Many are approved quickly, but the official advice is to allow 3 working days.

faq.q: Can I work with an ETA?
faq.a: No. It covers tourism, family visits and some short business activities, not employment.

esta.title: What is ESTA? US visa-waiver travel authorisation and fee (2026)
esta.metaDesc: ESTA is the online authorisation for the 42 Visa Waiver Program countries: $40.62, valid 2 years, stays up to 90 days. How to apply and who needs a visa instead.
esta.answer: ESTA is the online travel authorisation for citizens of the 42 countries in the US Visa Waiver Program. It costs $40.62, is valid for 2 years and allows stays of up to 90 days per entry. Nationals of other countries need a B1/B2 visa.

p: Citizens of the 42 Visa Waiver Program countries, including most EU countries, the UK, Japan, South Korea and Australia. You need an electronic (chip) passport.
If your country is not in the programme (for example Turkey, India or Brazil), you need a B1/B2 visa with a consulate interview.

list: Fee: $40.62 (since 16 October 2026; raised from $21 to $40 on 30 September 2025).
Valid for 2 years or until your passport expires.
Up to 90 days per entry; not for work or study.

p: Apply only on the official ESTA website or the ESTA Mobile app. Official advice: apply at least 72 hours before your flight. Third-party sites charge more for the same application.

list: Anyone who has been to Iran, Iraq, Libya, North Korea, Somalia, Sudan, Syria or Yemen since 1 March 2011, or to Cuba since 12 January 2021.
Dual nationals of Iran, Iraq, North Korea, Sudan, Syria or Cuba.
Travellers without an e-passport (with chip).
They apply for a B1/B2 visa instead.

p: The official fee is $40.62 since 16 October 2026; if refused, you still pay $10.62. Many sites ranking for 'ESTA application' charge several times more. Apply only on esta.cbp.dhs.gov or the ESTA Mobile app.

list: ESTA is required for land-border entry from Canada and Mexico since 1 October 2022.
Social media details are currently optional; a proposal to make them mandatory (December 2025) is not yet in force.
Check your status on esta.cbp.dhs.gov.

faq.q: How early should I apply for ESTA?
faq.a: At least 72 hours before departure; most applications are decided quickly.

faq.q: What if my ESTA is denied?
faq.a: You need to apply for a regular US visitor visa (B1/B2) at a consulate.

faq.q: Does ESTA guarantee entry?
faq.a: No. The final decision is made by the border officer on arrival.

greek_islands_visa.title: Greek islands visa on arrival for Turkish citizens (2026)
greek_islands_visa.metaDesc: Turkish citizens can visit 12 Greek islands with an express visa: up to 7 days, €60 state fee. Islands, documents, ports and rules explained.
greek_islands_visa.answer: Turkish citizens with ordinary passports can visit 12 Aegean Greek islands for up to 7 days with an express visa arranged through an agency or ferry company. The state fee is €60; with service charges the total is usually €75–85. The visa is valid only on the island you arrive at.

p: Rhodes, Kos, Samos, Lesbos, Chios, Leros, Symi, Lemnos, Kalymnos, Kastellorizo, Patmos and Samothrace. Santorini and Mykonos are not included.

list: Up to 7 days, single entry.
Valid only on the island you applied for; you cannot travel to other islands or mainland Greece.
The programme is extended from season to season; confirm the current status with the agency or ferry company before booking.
Holders of Turkish green and grey (special) passports already travel visa-free.
Passport valid for at least 6 more months (a copy is enough)
Biometric photo
Confirmed hotel booking
Travel health insurance with at least €30,000 cover
Bank statements for the last 3 months
Application form and passenger declaration

p: Apply through an authorised agency or ferry company and submit documents at least 7 working days before travel. Main routes: Marmaris/Fethiye–Rhodes, Bodrum–Kos, Kuşadası–Samos, Ayvalık–Lesbos, Çeşme–Chios, Kaş–Kastellorizo.

faq.q: How much does the express visa cost?
faq.a: The state fee is €60; with agency and ferry service charges the total is usually €75–85. Children under 12 pay no state fee.

faq.q: Can I visit Santorini with it?
faq.a: No. Santorini and Mykonos are not in the programme; they need a Schengen visa.

faq.q: Does it replace a Schengen visa?
faq.a: No. It is valid for up to 7 days on the island you applied for only.

visa_free_tr.title: Visa-free countries for Turkish passport holders 2026 (full list)
visa_free_tr.metaDesc: Turkish citizens can visit {free} countries visa-free in 2026, {id} of them with an ID card. Full list with stay limits, plus visa on arrival and eVisa countries.
visa_free_tr.answer: In 2026 holders of an ordinary Turkish passport can travel visa-free to {free} countries, {id} of which also accept the new chip Turkish ID card. Another {voa} countries issue a visa on arrival, {evisa} offer an eVisa and {eta} require an online travel authorisation (ETA) before the flight. The list below shows the stay limit for each country and updates with our data.

p: You enter with your passport and no prior application. Border officers may ask for a return or onward ticket and your accommodation.
The number of days is the longest single stay. Some countries also cap total days in a period (for example 90 days in any 180).

list: Most countries require your passport to be valid for at least 6 months after your return date.
ETA countries (South Korea K-ETA, Kenya eTA, Mexico) are not visa-free: apply online before you fly.
Some visa-free countries, such as Thailand, require a digital arrival card (TDAC).
Rules change: each country page links to the official source and shows when we last checked it.

sections.h: Why Schengen, the UK and the US are not on the list
p: Turkish citizens with an ordinary passport need a consular visa for the Schengen area, the UK, the US, Canada and China. Special (green) and service (grey) passports have different rules; this list is for ordinary passports.

faq.q: How many countries can Turkish citizens visit visa-free?
faq.a: In 2026, {free} countries with an ordinary passport. {voa} more give a visa on arrival, {evisa} offer an eVisa and {eta} require an online ETA.

faq.q: Which countries accept the Turkish ID card?
faq.a: {id} countries accept the new chip ID card; see the “ID card” group in the list. Some accept it only on direct flights, so read the note on the country page.

faq.q: Which European countries are visa-free for Turks?
faq.a: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, North Macedonia and Serbia in the Balkans, plus Georgia, Moldova, Ukraine and Azerbaijan. The Schengen area and the UK require a visa.

faq.q: Do I need travel insurance for visa-free trips?
faq.a: Most visa-free countries do not require it, but medical costs abroad can be very high. Some countries, such as Cuba, ask for health insurance at entry.

id_card_travel.title: Countries you can visit with an ID card instead of a passport (2026)
id_card_travel.metaDesc: Turkish chip ID card: Georgia, Azerbaijan, Moldova, Ukraine and Northern Cyprus. EU/EEA/Swiss ID cards: the EU, the Balkans, Georgia, Moldova and more. Conditions and sources.
id_card_travel.answer: With the new chip Turkish ID card you can enter Georgia, Azerbaijan, Moldova, Ukraine and Northern Cyprus without a passport. Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia do not accept it yet. EU, EEA and Swiss citizens can use their national ID card across the EU, the western Balkans, Georgia, Moldova and the European microstates, and some EU nationalities also in Türkiye.

sections.h: Turkish ID card: conditions by country
list: Georgia: stays up to 1 year. Travel health insurance (at least GEL 30,000) is mandatory since 1 January 2026.
Azerbaijan: up to 90 days, only on direct travel from Türkiye; the card must be valid for 30 days after entry.
Moldova: 90 days in any 180, only for travel between Türkiye and Moldova (since 19 February 2019).
Ukraine: 90 days in any 180 on paper, but there are no flights while the airspace is closed.
Northern Cyprus: up to 90 days with the chip card; old cards are not accepted since 30 June 2021.

p: ID-card agreements with both countries were signed in 2022 but never brought into force. Turkish citizens enter both visa-free for 90 days with a passport.

sections.h: EU, EEA and Swiss ID cards
p: Accepted in all EU/EEA countries and Switzerland, Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Serbia, Georgia, Moldova, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino and the Vatican. Montenegro accepts ID cards for stays of up to 30 days.

Türkiye accepts ID cards only from Belgium, Bulgaria, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Spain and Switzerland. Ukraine and the UK require a passport.

faq.q: Can Turkish citizens enter Bosnia with an ID card?
faq.a: No. The agreement is not in force; use a passport (90 days visa-free).

faq.q: Can Germans travel to Türkiye with a Personalausweis?
faq.a: Yes. German citizens can enter Türkiye with their ID card, and it may even be expired by up to one year.

faq.q: Is an ID card enough for Montenegro?
faq.a: For EU/EEA and Swiss citizens, yes, for stays of up to 30 days. Longer stays need a passport.

visa_fees.title: Visa fees 2026 for Turkish citizens: Schengen, UK, US and more
visa_fees.metaDesc: 2026 visa fees for Turkish citizens: Schengen €90, UK £135, US $185, Canada CAD 100 + CAD 85 biometrics, China TRY 1,225. Service centres (VFS, iDATA, BLS, Kosmos) and child fees.
visa_fees.answer: In 2026 the Schengen visa fee is €90 (€45 for children aged 6–12, free under 6), plus the service fee of the application centre (VFS Global, iDATA, BLS, Kosmos). A 6-month UK visitor visa costs £135, a US B1/B2 visa $185 and a Canadian visitor visa CAD 100 plus CAD 85 for biometrics. Japan is visa-free for up to 90 days.

p: The fee is the same for every Schengen country: €90 for adults, €45 for children aged 6–12, free under 6 (in force since 11 June 2024, unchanged in 2026). Centres may ask for the equivalent in TRY or USD.
Application centres also charge a service fee, which varies by centre; courier, SMS or premium lounge services are optional.

head: Country
Visa fee
Note
rows: Apply at VFS Global centres; decision usually in 3 weeks
Book via ustraveldocs.com; a $250 'visa integrity fee' was legislated, check the consulate for whether it is charged
Apply online; biometrics at VFS Ankara
Plus a service fee of TRY 2,530 (since 1 July 2026)

list: Pay only the official centre or consulate; never pay sites that sell appointments.
Fees are not refunded if the visa is refused.
Italy charges in TRY at a quarterly rate; Hungary waives the fee for Turkish citizens under 12.
Figures were checked against official pages on 5 November 2026; check the centre's fee page before applying.

faq.q: How much is a Schengen visa in 2026?
faq.a: €90 for adults, €45 for children aged 6–12, free under 6, plus the centre's service fee.

faq.q: Is the visa fee refunded if I am refused?
faq.a: No. Neither the visa fee nor the service fee is refunded.

visa_appointments.title: How to book a visa appointment and track your application from Türkiye (2026)
visa_appointments.metaDesc: Schengen, UK and US visa appointments from Türkiye: which centre handles each country (VFS, iDATA, BLS, Kosmos), booking and tracking addresses, when to apply and processing times.
visa_appointments.answer: Apply for a Schengen visa no earlier than 6 months and no later than 15 days before travel, at the centre of the country where you will stay longest. Germany and Italy use iDATA, Spain and Slovakia BLS, Greece Kosmos Vize, Hungary AS Visa and most others VFS Global. Decisions normally take 15 days, up to 45 if more checks are needed.

list: Apply 6 months to 15 days before travel; in spring and summer look for appointments 2–3 months ahead.
Several Schengen countries: apply to the one where you stay longest, or the first entry if stays are equal.
Processing takes 15 days, extendable to 45.
Germany: iDATA has used a waiting list since 18 March 2024; the embassy says tourist appointments can take from several months to a year.
Denmark: as of 4 November 2026 the embassy is processing files received by 2 September 2026.
United States: appointments moved to ustraveldocs.com on 30 May 2025.
Japan is visa-free for up to 90 days; Russia offers an e-visa (electronic-visa.kdmid.ru).

faq.q: How early can I apply for a Schengen visa?
faq.a: Up to 6 months before travel and no later than 15 days before.

faq.q: How long does a Schengen visa take?
faq.a: Normally 15 days, up to 45 if more checks are needed.

visa_free_ru.title: Visa-free countries for Russian passport holders 2026 (full list)
visa_free_ru.metaDesc: Russian citizens can visit {free} countries visa-free in 2026, {voa} with visa on arrival and {evisa} with an eVisa. China visa-free until 31 Dec 2027, Thailand 30 days, Schengen and US rules.
visa_free_ru.answer: In 2026 Russian passport holders can travel visa-free to {free} countries; {voa} more issue a visa on arrival, {evisa} offer an eVisa and {eta} require an electronic authorisation. China has extended visa-free stays of up to 30 days for Russians until 31 December 2027, and Thailand has allowed 30 days visa-free since 15 September 2026.

list: China: up to 30 days visa-free for tourism, business, family visits and transit, extended to 31 December 2027.
Thailand: 30 days visa-free since 15 September 2026 (was 60), extendable once by 30 days.
Georgia: health insurance of at least GEL 30,000 is mandatory since 1 January 2026.
Sri Lanka: free 30-day ETA since 25 May 2026.
Vietnam: 45 days visa-free.
Türkiye: 60 days per visit, max 90 in any 180.

p: Russians pay the full €90 Schengen fee since the EU suspended the visa facilitation agreement in 2022. Since 7 November 2025 Russians living in Russia normally receive single-entry visas only.
For US visas, Russian nationals are directed to the US embassies in Astana and Warsaw (since 6 September 2025); the B1/B2 fee is $185.

faq.q: Do Russians need a visa for China in 2026?
faq.a: No, for stays of up to 30 days; the visa-free policy runs until 31 December 2027.

faq.q: How long can Russians stay in Thailand without a visa?
faq.a: 30 days since 15 September 2026, extendable once by 30 days.

us_visa.title: US tourist visa (B1/B2) 2026: fee, DS-160, appointment and interview
us_visa.metaDesc: How to get a US B1/B2 visa in 2026: $185 fee, DS-160 form, booking the appointment in India, Mexico, Colombia, Argentina or Türkiye, interview waiver rules since October 2025, 10-year validity.
us_visa.answer: The US visitor visa (B1/B2) costs $185 in 2026. Fill in the DS-160, pay the fee, book your appointment in your country of nationality or residence and attend the interview. Since 1 October 2025 almost all applicants must interview in person; only some renewals can skip it. Citizens of India, Mexico, Colombia and Argentina usually receive a 10-year multiple-entry visa.

list: Complete the DS-160 online and keep the confirmation number.
Pay the $185 fee; the receipt is valid for about one year.
Book the appointment on your country's official system: ustraveldocs.com for India and Türkiye, ais.usvisa-info.com for Mexico, Colombia and Argentina.
Attend the interview with your passport and DS-160 confirmation.
Collect your passport or receive it by courier.

sections.h: Who can renew without an interview?
p: Since 1 October 2025 nearly everyone must interview, including children under 14 and adults over 79. You can renew without an interview only if your previous B1/B2 visa was issued for full validity, expired within the last 12 months, was issued when you were 18 or older, and you have no unresolved refusals.

A July 2025 law created an extra $250 fee charged at visa issuance. DHS said it will be implemented in a future publication, and we found no official notice that it is being collected yet. Check your embassy's fee page before paying.

The most common reason is section 214(b): the officer was not convinced of your ties to home (job, studies, family, property). It cannot be appealed, but you can reapply with a new DS-160 and fee, ideally when your circumstances have changed.

sections.h: Visa Waiver countries: ESTA instead of a visa
p: Citizens of Visa Waiver Program countries (most of the EU, the UK, Japan, Australia and others) apply for an ESTA online instead. The ESTA fee rose from $21 to $40 on 30 September 2025.

faq.q: How much is a US tourist visa in 2026?
faq.a: $185 for a B1/B2 visa. The extra $250 integrity fee has no official collection start date yet.

faq.q: Where can I check appointment wait times?
faq.a: On the State Department's official 'Visa Appointment Wait Times' tool on travel.state.gov.

uk_visa_india.title: UK visa for Indians 2026: fees, processing time, priority service and documents
uk_visa_india.metaDesc: UK Standard Visitor visa for Indian citizens in 2026: £135 for 6 months, 2/5/10-year visas £506/£903/£1,128, 3-week processing, priority £500 and super priority £1,000, documents and VFS centres.
uk_visa_india.answer: Indian citizens need a UK Standard Visitor visa (not an ETA). Since 8 April 2026 it costs £135 for up to 6 months; long-term visas cost £506 (2 years), £903 (5 years) and £1,128 (10 years). Decisions usually take 3 weeks; priority (£500) usually gives a decision within 5 working days and super priority (£1,000) by the end of the next working day. Apply online and give biometrics at a VFS Global centre in India, no earlier than 3 months before travel.

list: Apply online on gov.uk and pay the fee.
Book a biometrics appointment at a VFS Global UK visa centre; since May 2026 VFS also runs 12 optional paid Premium Application Centres (including Lucknow, Indore, Noida, Coimbatore and Guwahati).
You can apply up to 3 months before you travel.
A decision usually takes 3 weeks; priority services are offered when you apply if available.
A valid passport (and old passports showing travel history).
Proof you can pay for the trip: bank statements, salary slips, ITR.
Proof of ties to India: employment letter or business registration, leave approval, property or family ties.
Accommodation and trip details; an invitation letter if visiting family or friends.

sections.h: Do Indians need a UK ETA?
p: No. The ETA is only for visa-free nationalities. Indian citizens need a visitor visa.

faq.q: How much is a UK visa for Indians in 2026?
faq.a: £135 for a 6-month Standard Visitor visa (since 8 April 2026). Long-term visas: £506 for 2 years, £903 for 5 years, £1,128 for 10 years.

faq.q: How long does a UK visa take from India?
faq.a: Usually 3 weeks. Priority (£500) usually 5 working days; super priority (£1,000) usually the next working day.

dubai_visa_india.title: Dubai visa for Indians 2026: visa on arrival, e-visa fees and eligibility
dubai_visa_india.metaDesc: Dubai and UAE visa for Indian citizens in 2026: 14-day visa on arrival (AED 100) or 60 days (AED 250) for holders of US, UK, EU visas or residence, plus 30/60-day pre-arranged tourist visas and fees.
dubai_visa_india.answer: Indian citizens normally need a pre-arranged UAE tourist visa (30 or 60 days, single or multiple entry). Indians who also hold a valid US visa or green card, a UK visa or residence permit, an EU visa or residence permit, or a residence permit from Singapore, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand or Canada can get a visa on arrival: 14 days for AED 100 (extendable once by 14 days) or 60 days for AED 250. The passport and the other visa or permit must both be valid for at least 6 months.

list: Indian ordinary passport valid 6+ months, plus one of: US visa or green card; UK visa (including e-visa) or residence permit; EU visa or residence permit; residence permit from Singapore, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand or Canada (each valid 6+ months).
14 days for AED 100, extendable once inside the UAE for another 14 days.
60 days for AED 250, not extendable.

p: Visas can also be arranged through flydubai (with a flydubai booking, at least 5 working days ahead) or through UAE hotels and licensed agents. Prices vary by provider.

On 25 June 2026 the UAE extended the visa-on-arrival scheme, previously available only to Indians, to six more nationalities (Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, the Philippines, Kenya and South Africa). The rules for Indians stay the same.

faq.q: Can Indians get a visa on arrival in Dubai?
faq.a: Yes, if they also hold a valid US visa or green card, a UK or EU visa or residence permit, or a residence permit from Singapore, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand or Canada.

faq.q: How much is a Dubai tourist visa for Indians?
faq.a: Through Emirates, a 30-day single-entry visa costs about $90 and a 60-day single-entry visa about $177. Visa on arrival (if eligible) costs AED 100 for 14 days or AED 250 for 60 days.

thailand_india.title: Thailand visa for Indians 2026: 30 days visa-free, TDAC, e-visa and DTV
thailand_india.metaDesc: Thailand for Indian citizens in 2026: visa-free for 30 days since 15 September 2026 (was 60), free TDAC arrival card, tourist e-visa INR 3,000 for 60 days, Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) INR 30,000.
thailand_india.answer: Indian citizens can visit Thailand visa-free for tourism for up to 30 days. Thailand cut the visa-free stay from 60 to 30 days on 15 September 2026; travellers who entered before that keep their original permission. Every traveller must fill in the free Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) within 72 hours before arrival. For longer trips, apply online for a tourist e-visa (INR 3,000, 60 days) or the 5-year Destination Thailand Visa (INR 30,000, up to 180 days per stay).

head: Option
Cost
Stay
rows: Up to 180 days per entry (extendable once by 180 days), valid 5 years

p: Since 1 May 2025 every foreign arrival must submit the TDAC at tdac.immigration.go.th within 72 hours before arrival. It is free; beware of sites charging for it.

sections.h: Applying for an e-visa or DTV
list: All Thai visa applications from India go through the official portal thaievisa.go.th (mandatory since 1 January 2025).
The DTV is aimed at digital nomads, remote workers and freelancers, and people joining activities such as Muay Thai or cooking courses.
Apply well before travel and keep a printout of the approved e-visa.
Extend the visa exemption once: up to 30 more days at a Thai immigration office for 1,900 THB (at the officer's discretion).
Tourist visa (TR): 60 days, and it can be extended inside Thailand by another 30 days for 1,900 THB, so about 90 days in total.

DTV: 5-year multiple-entry visa for remote workers, freelancers and people doing Thai activities such as Muay Thai, cooking courses or medical treatment. Up to 180 days per entry, extendable by another 180 days; you need a bank balance of at least 500,000 THB.
Over land, visa-exempt entries are generally limited to two per calendar year, so repeated border runs no longer work well.

faq.q: Is Thailand visa-free for Indians in 2026?
faq.a: Yes, for tourism up to 30 days (reduced from 60 days on 15 September 2026).

faq.q: What is TDAC?
faq.a: The free Thailand Digital Arrival Card, required for every arrival since 1 May 2025 and submitted online within 72 hours before arrival.

schengen_india.title: Schengen visa for Indians 2026: fee, VFS, cascade rule and documents
schengen_india.metaDesc: Schengen visa from India in 2026: €90 fee (≈ ₹9,100), children 6–11 €45, VFS service charge on top, about 15 days processing, and the cascade rule that leads to 2- and 5-year multiple-entry visas.
schengen_india.answer: Indian citizens need a Schengen short-stay visa for trips of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. The visa fee is €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11 (under 6: free), paid in rupees, plus the service charge of the visa centre (VFS or BLS, roughly ₹400–3,100 depending on the country). Decisions normally take about 15 days, so book your appointment early: you can apply up to 6 months before travel. Since April 2024, Indians who have used two Schengen visas correctly within three years can receive a 2-year multiple-entry visa, normally followed by a 5-year one.

head: Item
Amount
rows: About 15 days, longer in peak season

sections.h: Which country should you apply to?
list: Apply to the country where you will spend the most nights; if equal, to the country you enter first.
Germany lets Indian applicants use any of its visa centres in India, which helps when Delhi or Mumbai slots are full.
Peak season (April–July and December) books out fast: check for new slots late at night and early in the morning.

p: Under an EU decision of April 2024, Indian nationals living in India who have obtained and lawfully used two Schengen visas within the previous three years can be issued a 2-year multiple-entry visa. After that, a 5-year visa is normally possible if the passport is valid long enough. It is not automatic: consulates still check each application.

list: Application form and two recent photos
Passport issued within the last 10 years, valid at least 3 months after your return, with 2 blank pages
Travel medical insurance with at least €30,000 cover for the whole Schengen area
Flight reservation and hotel bookings or an invitation
Bank statements for the last 3–6 months, ITRs and a leave letter or business documents

faq.q: How much is a Schengen visa for Indians in 2026?
faq.a: €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11, plus the visa centre service charge.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Usually about 15 days after your appointment; it can take longer in peak season.

faq.q: Can Indians get a 5-year Schengen visa?
faq.a: Yes, under the cascade rule: after two properly used visas in three years you can get a 2-year visa, and then normally a 5-year one.

japan_visa_india.title: Japan visa for Indians 2026: eVISA, ₹500 fee, VFS and processing time
japan_visa_india.metaDesc: Japan visa for Indian citizens in 2026: tourist eVISA via VFS since April 2024, visa fee ₹500 plus VFS charge, processing about 5 working days, stays of up to 90 days.
japan_visa_india.answer: Indian citizens need a visa for Japan. For tourism the easiest route is the Japan eVISA, available to Indians since 1 April 2024: you still submit documents at a VFS Japan Visa Application Centre, but the visa is issued electronically and shown on your phone at arrival. The consular fee for Indians is ₹500 (applications from 1 July 2026 to 31 March 2027), plus the VFS service charge. Processing usually takes about 5 working days, and a short-term visa allows stays of up to 90 days.

head: Item
Details
rows: Up to 90 days, decided by the embassy

list: Book at a VFS Japan Visa Application Centre in your jurisdiction (visa.vfsglobal.com/ind/en/jpn/).
Since 2 March 2026 appointments are mandatory in Chennai, Cochin, Hyderabad and Puducherry; rules differ by centre, so check yours.
Carry: passport, application form, photo, flight and hotel plan, bank statements and ITRs.
With an eVISA, keep the visa notice on your phone; it is checked at check-in and at Japanese immigration.

p: Japan offers multiple-entry visas to Indian nationals who travel often, such as business travellers or people with a good Japan travel history. Requirements are stricter than for a single-entry visa; check the embassy or consulate page for your jurisdiction.

faq.q: Can Indians get a Japan e-visa?
faq.a: Yes. Since April 2024 the Japan eVISA is available to Indian nationals for short-term tourism, applied for through VFS.

faq.q: How much is the Japan visa fee for Indians?
faq.a: ₹500 for applications between 1 July 2026 and 31 March 2027, plus the VFS service charge.

faq.q: How long does a Japan visa take from India?
faq.a: Usually about 5 working days after the application is accepted.

vietnam_visa_india.title: Vietnam visa for Indians 2026: e-visa $25, 90 days, official site and Phu Quoc
vietnam_visa_india.metaDesc: Vietnam e-visa for Indian citizens in 2026: up to 90 days, $25 single or $50 multiple entry, about 3 working days on the official evisa.gov.vn. Phu Quoc is visa-free for 30 days.
vietnam_visa_india.answer: Indian citizens need a visa for mainland Vietnam. Apply online for an e-visa on the official portal evisa.gov.vn: it allows stays of up to 90 days and costs $25 for single entry or $50 for multiple entry. Processing usually takes about 3 working days (5–7 in peak periods). Phu Quoc island is visa-free for 30 days if you fly or sail there directly from abroad and stay on the island.

p: The official portals are evisa.gov.vn and thithucdientu.gov.vn. Many lookalike agency sites charge several times the government fee. Check the spelling of your name and passport number carefully: a mistake means a new application.

list: Visa-free entry applies only when you arrive directly in Phu Quoc from abroad and stay on the island.
If you plan to visit the mainland too, get an e-visa.
In April 2026 the Indian Embassy in Hanoi advised travellers to carry a proper visa to avoid problems.

faq.q: Is Vietnam visa-free for Indians?
faq.a: No, except Phu Quoc island (30 days, direct arrival). For the rest of Vietnam you need an e-visa.

faq.q: How much is the Vietnam e-visa for Indians?
faq.a: $25 for single entry and $50 for multiple entry, for up to 90 days.

faq.q: How long does the Vietnam e-visa take?
faq.a: Usually about 3 working days; allow up to a week in peak periods.
